Platform architecture Stable

Read the platform through its users, responsibilities, components, and operation sequences. These diagrams describe the implementation, not an inventory of deployed AWS resources.

Reading order

Start with 05 System context → 04 Use cases in the Draw.io source. Then read the views below. Use 01 SaaS / 02 Lite / 03 Local for physical placement and wiring.

The developer architecture guide links each operation to its source files, completion criteria, and failure diagnostics. The shared diagrams use Japanese labels alongside implementation names.

Cloud responsibilities

SaaS uses SBT to manage tenants. Lite omits that tenant-management layer. Pooled and silo describe where organizer applications are placed, not additional logical responsibilities. The boxes do not correspond one-to-one to CDK stacks or AWS accounts.

Cloud components

Event APIs, deployment workflows, participant APIs, the coordination dispatcher, and scheduled scoring have different owners. Tenant isolation combines request authentication and scope checks with storage keys and stack boundaries. Supported Turso configurations update deployment state through the StatusWriter Lambda; Step Functions does not connect directly to SQL.

Local play and Docker

make local is a personal-practice path with a fixed local event and team. The control container and problem containers run under the same Docker daemon. Problem correctness is checked through HTTP /verify, progress is saved in SQLite, and containers are started and stopped through the Docker socket. A read-only socket mount does not make Docker API operations read-only.

The in-development multi-team local host and the crypto-battle development harness are separate paths. The make local-dev Simulator is enabled only by explicit opt-in; Docker problems do not require it.

SaaS tenant onboarding

Registration acceptance is separate from tenant readiness. Check the SBT lifecycle result. PLATINUM deploys a dedicated stack; other tiers use the existing pooled stack.

Problem deployment

This shows the AWS Lambda deployment path. HTTP acceptance counts are not successful deployment counts. Check each deployment job's COMPLETE or FAILED result. The guide describes the Distributed Map alternative and the omitted CodeBuild path.

Cloud answers and scoring

Flag submission and coordination operations use separate paths. Coordination state persistence and score delivery are also separate: pending scores are saved and delivery is retried. Scheduled scoring is triggered independently of participant submissions.

Local play startup and scoring

Starting a problem returns 202 before the actual Docker startup completes. Answers are checked by the problem verifier, then progress is persisted before the response. Verifier connection failures remain errors; they are not converted to incorrect answers or success.

Passing Turso tests does not verify a live event or its bill. SaaS's SBT DynamoDB resources and Lite's control-data configuration have different boundaries.
